goal: Enable the -Wunused-const-variable compiler warning in the build and fix all the header constants that currently trigger it.
reviewability: Not reviewable yet: the leveldb, minisketch, and crc32c commits are marked nomerge and depend on separate upstream subtree PRs merging first, and CI is currently failing.

categories.name: build
why: P4 because it only adds a new warning flag and fixes the resulting unused-variable warnings, a hygiene improvement with no user-facing effect.
Part of a larger effort (#36167) to enable -Wunused warnings across the codebase.

result.summary: This PR adds -Wunused-const-variable to the CMake warning set and converts a batch of `static const` / `constexpr` header constants to `inline constexpr` across leveldb, crc32c, minisketch, logging.h, and mempool_estimator.h so the new warning does not fire. Several commits are explicitly marked [nomerge] because they mirror changes proposed in separate upstream subtree PRs (leveldb-subtree #65, minisketch #105, crc32c-subtree #10) that need to land first. It is a draft split out of the broader #36167 RFC to enable -Wunused warnings.
result.problem: Unused constant definitions in headers currently escape detection; enabling this warning (and eventually -Werror) would catch such dead code, but first every existing header constant needs to be made inline-safe so the warning does not spuriously fire across the whole codebase and subtrees.
